name: Esterhazy torte
origin: Named for the Hungarian Esterházy noble family; layers of hazelnut (or walnut) meringue-dacquoise sandwiched with vanilla buttercream, the top traditionally finished with a spiderweb pattern in white and dark icing.

ingredients.note: ground hazelnut, not wheat flour, is the real structural base of a dacquoise; no ground-hazelnut substance record exists yet (see catalog.ts module notes)
a small amount of wheat flour is a common stabiliser in this style of nut meringue

process.name: whip whites
process.description: whip egg whites to soft peaks

process.name: add sugar
process.description: add sugar gradually to a stiff, glossy meringue

process.name: fold in nut flour
process.description: fold in the ground hazelnut and wheat flour

process.name: spread thin discs and bake
process.description: spread into thin discs and bake until dry and lightly coloured, without deep browning

notes: A dacquoise-family nut meringue: no fat at all in the baked layers themselves (real and correctly zero — the richness in the finished torte comes entirely from the buttercream between layers), close to the same egg-white-to-sugar ratio as a classic French meringue. The vanilla buttercream filling and the spiderweb icing finish are separately-prepared components, out of scope for this formulation.
